oracle_price_stale_at_market_creation.meaning: the pull-based oracle price is stale (lagging) at the time a market is created
oracle_price_stale_at_market_creation.checkpoint: before market creation / initMarket price read

oracle_update_before_initial_price_read.meaning: the pull-based oracle is updated before any initial price read during market initialization
oracle_update_before_initial_price_read.checkpoint: during market initialization, before initial price read

initial_price_read_occurred.meaning: an initial price read occurs during market initialization

arbitrage_price_gap_at_initialization_oc.meaning: an attacker creates a market while the oracle lags and then immediately performs mint/redeem/swap (refreshing to the true price) to arbitrage the price gap established at initialization
arbitrage_price_gap_at_initialization_oc.checkpoint: after market creation and subsequent mint/redeem/swap

assumptions: The oracle update and the initial price read are observable events during market initialization.

unresolved.description: The intent requires the oracle update to occur before the initial price read; the report does not give a numeric timestamp or ordering value, so the ordering is encoded as two occurrence symbols with a strict temporal_order relation rather than a numeric comparison.

limitations: The impact is potential; the impact_outcome Boolean records the reported scenario rather than asserting it is inevitable.
The arbitrage magnitude and the exact price gap are not numerically specified in the report.

links.reported_relation: initMarket reads the price immediately without calling _updateOraclePrice first, so a stale oracle makes the market born mispriced.
A subsequent mint/redeem/swap updates to the correct price and unlocks a deterministic arbitrage of the mispricing.
